newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany plans strategic oil reserve sale - Rexrodt.
newsitem.headline: Germany plans strategic oil reserve sale - Rexrodt.

text.p: Germany still plans to sell 7.3 million tonnes of oil from its strategic reserves in stages to help relieve strained government finances, Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt was reported on Thursday as saying.
Rexrodt was quoted by the Handelsblatt business daily saying the oil stocks were worth some 1.4 billion marks.
Offering petroleum for sale could raise around 500 million marks a year in both 1997 and 1998, but Rexrodt said the sale would not have an impact on the world oil market.

Bonn is searching for ways to cut its budget deficit this year and next to meet the strict borrowing requirements for European economic and monetary union. The German government also wants to force the pace of privatisation, even though the Maastricht treaty does not allow the proceeds to be taken into account when calculating budget deficits.

Western countries built up strategic oil reserves following the 1970s Arab oil embargo to try and shield themselves from any oil price shocks. But, with oil prices moderate since the 1990-1991 Gulf crisis, that threat appears to have receded.
